newsitem.title: GERMANY: German May BME/Reuters PMI adj. 57.49 vs 56.58.
newsitem.headline: German May BME/Reuters PMI adj. 57.49 vs 56.58.

text.p: The BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index rose to a seasonally-adjusted 57.49 in May from 56.58 in April, research group NTC Publications Ltd said in a statement released on Monday.
On an unadjusted basis it fell to 57.42 from 57.93.

The index, launched last month and available exclusively on Reuters systems, shows that on a seasonally-adjusted basis manufacturing activity expanded for the ninth consecutive month in May, NTC said.
The index also shows an acceleration in the pace of growth, mounting evidence of bottlenecks and resulting price rises, and a halt in the overall decline in employment, NTC said.

The index is based on a survey of 350 companies carried out exclusively for Reuters by research group NTC Publications Ltd in cooperation with the BME German Association for Materials Management, Purchasing and Logistics.
NOTE - The PMI, modelled on the closely watched U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index, was launched last month.

A reading below 50 percent indicates that the manufacturing economy is generally declining, while a level above 50 percent shows it generally expanding. The more it deviates from 50, the greater the improvement or decline in the current month.
